facts.fact: Interest on opening capital Rs 2,00,000 at 8% for the full year = Rs 16,000
Interest on additional capital Rs 50,000 at 8% for 9 months (1 July to 31 March) = Rs 3,000
Interest is lost on the Rs 30,000 withdrawn for 6 months (1 Oct to 31 March) = Rs 1,200; total = 16,000 + 3,000 - 1,200 = Rs 17,800

reason: The old bank only computes interest on one capital for a full year (e.g. Rs 1,30,000 x 6%); no old bank question time-weights an addition and a withdrawal of capital.

facts.fact: Interest on capital is an appropriation and is allowed only out of profits
Total interest due = 8% of 3,00,000 + 8% of 4,00,000 = 24,000 + 32,000 = Rs 56,000, which exceeds the profit of Rs 14,000
When profit is insufficient, the profit is shared in the ratio of interest on capital (24,000:32,000 = 3:4), so Ansh gets 3/7 of 14,000 = Rs 6,000

reason: The old bank has interest on capital only where profit is enough; no old bank question shares an insufficient profit in the ratio of interest on capital.

facts.fact: At retirement, assets and liabilities are revalued through the Revaluation Account
Partners' current account balances are then transferred to their capital accounts
The capital accounts are then settled, and the Balance Sheet is prepared last

reason: Old material lists revaluation as an aspect of retirement, but nothing states that current accounts are closed into capital accounts before the capital accounts and then the balance sheet.

facts.fact: AS 26 is the Accounting Standard on intangible assets and defines an intangible asset as identifiable, non-monetary, without physical existence and held for use in production, rental or administration

reason: Old cards mention AS 26 only for internally generated goodwill and define intangible assets without naming a standard; nothing says AS 26 is the standard on intangible assets.

facts.fact: Super profit = Goodwill / years of purchase = 30,000 / 3 = Rs 10,000
Normal profit = Average profit - Super profit = 60,000 - 10,000 = Rs 50,000
Normal rate of return = Normal profit / Capital employed x 100 = 50,000 / 5,00,000 = 10%

reason: Old bank goodwill questions go forward from the normal rate to goodwill; none works back from goodwill to the normal rate of return.

facts.fact: On death, the deceased partner's share of profit up to the date of death may be estimated on the basis of sales (turnover)
Profit to sales ratio of last year = 50,000 / 4,00,000 = 12.5%
Profit from 1 April to 30 June 2025 = 12.5% of sales 75,000 = Rs 9,375

reason: The old bank only apportions profit to the date of death on a time basis (212dadfc); no old bank question uses the sales basis.

facts.fact: Revaluation changes: Patents 11,000 to 8,000 = loss 3,000; Machinery 30,000 to 28,000 = loss 2,000; Buildings 20,000 to 25,000 = gain 5,000
Net revaluation = 5,000 - 3,000 - 2,000 = 0, so no profit and no loss

reason: No old bank question nets several asset revaluations into a revaluation profit or loss; the old rows only split a given revaluation gain or loss.

facts.fact: Intangible assets are written off within an estimated life not exceeding 10 years: (A)-(II)
AS 26 deals with intangible assets: (B)-(III)
Section 37 gives the outgoing partner the option of 6% interest or a share of profits: (C)-(IV)
facts.quote: the outgoing partner has an option to receive either interest @ 6% p.a. till the date of payment or such share of profits which has been earned with his/her money

facts.fact: Section 4 of the Indian Partnership Act 1932 defines partnership: (D)-(I)

reason: Old cards teach Section 37 and Section 4, but nothing states the 10-year write-off of intangible assets or that AS 26 deals with intangible assets.

facts.fact: Remaining share after Z = 1 - 1/4 = 3/4, split 2:1, so X new = 1/2 and Y new = 1/4
Sacrifice = old share - new share: X = 3/5 - 1/2 = 1/10; Y = 2/5 - 1/4 = 3/20
facts.quote: Old shares 15/25 and 10/25 becoming 12/25 and 8/25 means sacrifices of 3/25 and 2/25 respectively, i.e., 3:2.

facts.fact: Sacrificing ratio = 1/10 : 3/20 = 2:3

reason: Old bank admission questions always keep the old partners' old ratio, so their sacrifice ratio equals the old ratio; none gives the old partners a new mutual ratio and works the sacrifice out from it.

facts.fact: Adjusted profits = actual profits - partners' salary 12,000: 18,000, 24,000, 30,000
Normal profit = 15% of 1,00,000 = 15,000
Super profit, average of 3 years = 24,000 - 15,000 = 9,000; goodwill at 2 years = 18,000
Super profit, average of last 2 years = 27,000 - 15,000 = 12,000; goodwill at 3 years = 36,000; the lower, Rs 18,000, is taken

reason: The old bank computes super profit only from a given average profit; no old bank question deducts partners' salary from past profits or compares two bases.

facts.fact: Amount to be paid in shares = 1,90,000 - 10,000 cash = Rs 1,80,000
Issue price per share = 100 + 20% premium = Rs 120
Number of shares = 1,80,000 / 120 = 1,500

reason: No old bank question finds the number of shares issued to a vendor at a premium (e447dd1e gives the number of shares at par).

facts.fact: Debentures issued = 99,000 / 90 = 1,100 debentures of Rs 100 = Rs 1,10,000 face value
Entry: P Ltd. Dr 99,000 and Discount on Issue of Debentures Dr 11,000, To 12% Debentures 1,10,000

reason: No old bank question issues debentures to a vendor at a discount; the old card gives the entry only, and a card does not cover a numerical.

facts.fact: Application: Bank Dr 1,25,000 (5,000 x 25) To Debenture Application
Allotment due 5,000 x 45 = 2,25,000, credited 1,75,000 to Debentures and 50,000 to Securities Premium Reserve; received 2,25,000, not 2,20,000
First and final call: Bank Dr 2,00,000 (5,000 x 40)

reason: No old bank question records debentures issued at a premium payable by application, allotment and call.

facts.fact: Application money = 110 - 60 - 20 = Rs 30 per share, the only amount paid
Amount forfeited = 200 x 30 = Rs 6,000 (unpaid premium is not forfeited)
Discount on reissue at Rs 70 as fully paid = 30 x 200 = Rs 6,000, set off against the forfeited amount
facts.quote: On reissue at Rs 8, the discount allowed is Rs 2 x 1,000 = Rs 2,000, which is set off against the forfeited amount.

facts.fact: Capital reserve = 6,000 - 6,000 = Nil

reason: Old bank forfeiture questions are at par with the paid amount given; none works out the paid amount on shares issued at a premium with unpaid premium excluded.

facts.fact: Stock taken over by partner = 50% of 35,000 = 17,500 at 10% less = Rs 15,750, which brings no cash
Remaining stock 17,500 sold at a 15% gain = Rs 20,125 cash

reason: No old bank question works out the cash realised when a partner takes over part of an asset and the rest is sold at a gain.

facts.fact: Interest on long-term debt = 15% of 20,00,000 = Rs 3,00,000
Interest coverage ratio = (PBT + interest) / interest = 5,00,000 / 3,00,000 = 1.67 times

reason: The old bank has no interest coverage ratio question; an old card has the formula only, which does not cover a numerical.

Copy from the Home tab
Choose Paste Special from Paste
Select Values in the Paste Special box and click OK
